page: OVHcloud l40s-180 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 30 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9124 processor with an x86_64 architecture running at 2.75 GHz. The system is equipped with 180 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in large language model (LLM) inference tasks. Prompt processing and text generation speeds across small, medium, and large models consistently rank in the top 10% of tested systems. CPU-bound operations also demonstrate strong capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is mixed, showing strong read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks but falling into the middle 50% for larger uncached read and write blocks.

From a resource density perspective, the l40s-180 offers a balanced profile for parallelized workloads. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores lack hyperthreading, which limits concurrent thread scaling but ensures predictable, non-shared execution performance. The inclusion of dual L40S GPUs makes this server highly efficient for AI inference, machine learning model fine-tuning, and graphics rendering, avoiding the higher costs associated with enterprise-grade A100 or H100 deployments. It is highly suited for LLM serving, database operations, and high-throughput cryptographic processing.
